title: Opening Bell Boss
bigIdea: Put Unit 1 together: ownership, prices, stock cards, and trades in one trading day.

cards.title: Boss battle
cards.body: This brings Unit 1 together. Answer a quick gauntlet, then trade through a fictional opening bell. Beat it to earn the Rookie rank.

steps.prompt: A share of a company gives you what?

options.text: A small slice of ownership in that company
A promise of a fixed monthly payment
A discount on the company's products

steps.explanation: A share is a slice of ownership, not a loan or a coupon.

steps.prompt: When many more buyers than sellers want in, the price tends to rise.
steps.explanation: More demand than supply pushes buyers to compete, which lifts the price.

steps.prompt: You place a market order to buy. What should you expect?

options.text: It fills right away at about the current price
It fills only if the price falls to your target
It never fills on a busy day

steps.explanation: A market order trades now at roughly the current price.

steps.prompt: A gain on a stock you still hold is realized profit you can spend.
steps.explanation: A gain you have not sold is unrealized. It becomes realized only when you sell.

steps.goal: Trade a 90-second fictional day. Read each headline, pick the best interpretation, then make a practice move. (Simulation.)

events.headline: ACME reports record sales, far above what analysts expected.

interpretations.text: A big positive surprise that could lift the price
Bad news, because sales should always be higher

events.explanation: Beating expectations by a lot is a positive surprise, which often pushes a price up.

events.headline: ACME warns next quarter may be slower than it had guided.

interpretations.text: A warning about the future that could weigh on the price
Great news that guarantees the price rises

events.explanation: A warning about weaker results ahead is a negative signal, even after a good day.

events.headline: A rival launches a copycat product at a lower price.

interpretations.text: New competition that could pressure ACME

events.explanation: A cheaper rival product is competition that can pressure sales and the price.

events.headline: ACME's results met expectations exactly, with no surprises.

interpretations.text: Roughly in line, so a small or quiet reaction is likely
A huge surprise that will swing the price hard

events.explanation: Prices react to surprises. Meeting expectations exactly usually brings a muted move.

events.headline: A rumor spreads online with no source or evidence.

interpretations.text: An unverified rumor to treat with caution
A confirmed fact to act on immediately

events.explanation: An unsourced rumor is not confirmed news. Caution beats rushing to trade on it.

steps.prompt: Pick the best explanation of why a company's price can fall even after good news.

options.text: The good news was still weaker than what people already expected
Good news always makes prices fall
Prices move completely at random and never follow news

steps.explanation: Prices move on surprises versus expectations. If results are good but below what the crowd expected, the price can still drop.
